messages:
maya: thinking out loud — can we add an operator inbox for automatic fallback events? right now alerts are noisy and scattered.
ara: yes please. current console floods with low-priority fallbacks during deploys. grouping + dedupe would help a lot. :pray:
sam: what do people want in that inbox? i’d keep it compact: route, model, reason, sample req_id, and link to runbook.
li: +1. also need a way to distinguish 'soft' degradations (latency-based sampling) vs 'hard' failovers (5xx or OOM).
tess: UX idea: show a single aggregated card per incident with counters and a 1-click expand to see samples. hide repeated identical reasons after N occurrences.
maya: agree. we should support severity tags: notice/warning/critical. severity computed from trigger (p95>2s for >5m => warning; 5xx ratio >2% => critical).
ara: what about operator actions? quick buttons: ACK, SNOOZE 1h, ESCALATE, REROUTE (to fallback model). ACK should write to audit log with actor + reason.
li: audit log must include human-readable explanation, original trigger metrics snapshot, and a few example request traces. retention 90d by default.
sam: API-wise we need an endpoint to fetch grouped events: GET /v1/fallback-inbox?route=...&state=open&group_by=reason. response should include sample_request_ids.
tess: also add an operator 'simulate revert' that runs in dry-run — shows what traffic would look like if we rerouted. no actual change unless operator confirms.
maya: ops-bot: can you add runbook link template when a runbook exists? e.g., runbook://{service}/{playbook} so inbox links are stable.
ops-bot: Added suggestion: runbook links supported. Also propose a 'quiet mode' so teams can opt-out of low-severity noise during planned deploy windows.
ara: one more: we need to surface the fallback policy version and hash in the card so auditors can see which policy executed.
li: and add a 'why' explainability field: short machine-generated sentence — e.g., "Fallback triggered by sustained latency increase on model-x, fallback -> model-y due to capacity."
sam: for privacy, sample payloads should be sanitized and only include metadata + small truncated input. we already do this elsewhere.
tess: implementation note: frontend should fetch streaming updates to keep the card counters live. we can reuse the telemetry websocket used by the console.
maya: next steps: design mockups + API contract. @ara can you own a short proto for GET /v1/fallback-inbox and the ACK POST body?
ara: on it. will draft by EOD tomorrow and share a Figma. :thumbsup:
li: quick question — should ACK hide the card or just mark it acknowledged? i'd prefer keep visible but marked, so history remains.
maya: keep visible (marked). allow dismiss separately. ack should be reversible by admins.
ess: +1
ops-bot: NOTE: this thread will be archived into the eng-platform backlog under "fallback-inbox" once @ara posts the proto.
maya: thanks everyone. small follow-up: include sampling rate in the card so we know if this is 1% sampled or full traffic.
ara: noted. will include sampling_rate and snapshot_metrics in the proto.
li: great work. this should cut down on paging noise and make audits easier.
maya: closing for now — will follow up with the proto. :sparkles:
